Fees & incentives · initial research

Who pays, and who gets paid.

What the holder pays, and how the issuer, custodian and other parties earn from the product.

The headline fee is one cost among several. Spreads, recurring deductions, lending income and exit costs also affect what a holder pays over time.

What we are trying to establish

01

The holder’s cost path

Entering, holding, moving, using in DeFi and exiting. Keep network charges, underlying fund expenses and taxes separate from issuer revenue.

02

The actor’s business model

Who pays whom? Fixed contracts, assets under management, trading volume, spreads, performance, lending or liquidation income. Who bears the losses?

03

The long-term arrangement

Who benefits from keeping the product useful? Who can raise fees, change providers or end it? What changes when assets or trading volumes shrink?

How to read this first edition

These are research profiles per programme, with the product and route each applies to. They do not quote every fee for every token. A permission to charge a fee does not mean the fee is charged. A fee ceiling is a maximum; the current fee may be lower. A key that can withdraw fees does not identify the legal beneficiary.

Our notes on each party's incentives are analysis. They do not claim intent or misconduct. Knowing who takes part in a product does not tell us how they are paid. If we have not researched a point, that does not mean the issuer failed to disclose it.

Source dates remain attached to the underlying evidence. A newly generated page does not make an old observation current. This first edition is curated; it does not add a new collector or automatically refresh its conclusions. Follow source changes in Changes.

This is research. It is not investment, legal or tax advice. Inspect the structured data →
